newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court sends back Bhutto challenge.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court sends back Bhutto challenge.

text.p: Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday sent back ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's petition against her sacking, saying it contained "objectionable and scandalous portions", court and legal sources said.

A court official declined to specify the objectionable portions. Bhutto's lawyer, Aitzaz Ahsan, said he was surprised by the court action on the petition, which he filed last Wednesday to challenge her dismissal by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
The 42-page petition had contained blistering criticism of Leghari for dismissing his former political patron and dissolving the National Assembly (lower house of parliament).
"I have also heard (about the return of the petition), Ahsan told Reuters by telephone from his office in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore.
"The specific objection of the office of the Supreme Court has not been brought to my notice as yet," he said. "I am no doubt surprised."
Asked if he would remove the objectionable portions and file the petition again, Ahsan said he would come to Islamabad on Wednesday to see what to do next.
